required_fixes: The frozen decision rule's S6 (complementarity) threshold is correct but the experimental design does not discriminate: reconstruction rule (choose_adoptions+rewrite_template_multi) makes coverage 1.0 for ANY non-empty candidate set because observed alias key is never in registry union. This masks all retrieval/mining differences including WebAPI vs hierarchical vs flat vs random. To test complementarity, either (a) disable reconstruction and test verbatim bind, or (b) require correct-family candidate for rewrite, or (c) test on live substrate where reconstruction may fail.

The WebAPI endpoint mining pipeline produces IDENTICAL outcomes to hierarchical retrieval on every measured dimension (correct_rate 0.975, coverage 1.0, density 1.385, ECE 0.1389, theme selections, entropy traces). The 'endpoint discovery' layer is functionally equivalent to hierarchical theme retrieval on this synthetic data. No evidence supports 'higher-leverage' claim.

The held-out auth failure (alias-2-7, 1/40) affects WebAPI, hierarchical, and flat equally. This is not a WebAPI-specific issue but indicates the registry expansion (pool 8) still has a minor gap for held-out auth forms. Not a measurement validity threat but worth noting for replication.
validity_findings: RECONSTRUCTION CONFOUND (Critical): The genuine reconstruction rule (adopt-any-observed-key-not-in-registry + rewrite_template_multi alphabetically-sorted multi-adoption) is too powerful for this synthetic design. Because test tasks use held-out alias forms (X-Api-Key, api_token, X-Scope, etc.) that by design do not appear in the training registry, ANY retrieved candidate can be rewritten to the correct bound action. This yields recall@k=1.0 for ALL pipelines including B-RANDOM-K5 (39/40). Coverage gain is structurally 0.0 regardless of retrieval quality. The pool saturation fix (registry 8 > k=5) is necessary but not sufficient; the reconstruction bottleneck masks retrieval differences. This is a design-level validity threat acknowledged in producer validity_notes and unresolved.

WEB_API VS HIERARCHICAL EQUIVALENCE: Raw evidence shows H-WEBAPI-ENDPOINT-MINING and H-HIERARCHICAL-XMEMORY produce identical per-task outcomes: same retrieved_ids, same themes_selected, same theme_types_selected, same entropy_trace, same coverage_trace, same expansion_steps, same k_cap_reason. The WebAPI 'endpoint catalog' is derived from the same registry mechanisms and uses identical component parsing, Jaccard clustering (threshold 0.6), centroid scoring, and top-down complementary selection. The only difference is terminology (endpoint vs mechanism, endpoint themes vs themes). On this synthetic data, they are the same algorithm with different labels.

NO COMPLEMENTARITY SIGNAL: Coverage gain WebAPI vs best flat = 0.0 (bootstrap CI [0.0, 0.0], p=1.0). Density gain = -0.03 (p=0.85). Hierarchical vs flat gain = 0.0. The producer's own validity_notes confirm: 'Coverage gain 0.0 is not due to pool<=k (pool 8>k fixed) but due to reconstruction adopting any observed key not in union, making recall 1.0 for any non-empty set'. This is a correct diagnosis.

CALIBRATION: WebAPI ECE 0.1389 (5 bins) bootstrap CI [0.08, 0.18] upper <=0.18 passes S4. However, 3 of 5 confidence bins are empty (bimodal confidence distribution), and std=0.092. This is a known limitation of synthetic data where confidence is derived from softmax over candidate scores with temp 0.15. Calibration transfer to live data is unsubstantiated.

NO ORACLE LEAK: NC-ORACLE-LEAK passes. Forbidden keys (alias_family, query_key, target_prefix, etc.) absent from derived_context. Confidence std >0.05 for retrieval pipelines (TFIDF 0.091, EMBED 0.093, hier 0.092, webapi 0.092). Component/endpoint extraction uses only template string parsing. Index manifests auditable with no forbidden keys.

CONTROLS PASS: All positive controls (PC-EXACT-MATCH, PC-RETRIEVAL-HEALTH, PC-WEBAPI-INDEX-BUILT, PC-ENDPOINT-DISCOVERY-SANITY) and null controls (NC-NO-APPLICABLE, NC-EMPTY-REGISTRY, NC-ORACLE-LEAK) pass. No harness errors, no registry/endpoint leak. Measurement validity is intact.

SYNTHETIC-TO-REAL GAP: No BrowserGym 1280x720 live substrate, no AX tree, no production SPA. Claim explicitly bounded to 'synthetic orthogonal header/body/auth + mixed multi-channel aliasing with minimal derived dict'. This is correctly disclosed but limits generalizability.

MIXED STRATUM: 10/10 correct for WebAPI but this is expected under reconstruction confound. Mixed tasks require joint header+body+query rewriting; reconstruction handles this via multi-adoption. No evidence that WebAPI's endpoint discovery provides specific advantage for multi-channel composition.
baseline_findings: B-EXACT-MATCH: 0/40 alias-OOD, 1.0 false_accept (expected, validates aliasing breaks exact matching). 12/12 exact-match. PASS.
B-VERBATIM-REPLAY: 0/40 alias-OOD, 1.0 false_accept (expected, validates negative transfer harm). PASS.
B-FLAT-RAG-TFIDF-K5: 39/40 0.975 pooled, coverage 1.0, density 1.49. Strong lexical baseline with reconstruction. PASS.
B-FLAT-RAG-EMBED-K5: 39/40 0.975 pooled, coverage 1.0, density 1.44. Strong semantic baseline with reconstruction (all-MiniLM-L6-v2 available). PASS.

B-FLAT-RAG-EMBED-K1: 38/40 0.95 coverage (verbatim bind, no reconstruction). This ablation shows retrieval alone has some discrimination (0.95 vs 0.0 for exact), but K5+reconstruction restores 0.975 for all. PASS.

B-RANDOM-K5: 39/40 0.975 pooled, coverage 1.0, density 1.685. Random retrieval + reconstruction achieves same as best flat/hierarchical/WebAPI. This is the smoking gun for reconstruction confound. PASS as baseline but invalidates retrieval complementarity test.
H-HIERARCHICAL-XMEMORY (comparator): 39/40 0.975 pooled, coverage 1.0, density 1.385, 84 themes. Reused byte-identical from parent EXP-FRONTIER-35782552659. PASS.

H-WEBAPI-ENDPOINT-MINING (experimental): 39/40 0.975 pooled, orthogonal 29/30 0.967, mixed 10/10 1.0, heldout 8/9 0.889, coverage 1.0, density 1.385, ECE 0.1389, false_accept 0.025. IDENTICAL to hierarchical on all dimensions. PASS as implementation but FAILS to show higher leverage.
All baselines are correctly implemented and strong. The problem is not baseline weakness but experimental insensitivity due to reconstruction confound.
claim_ceiling: WebAPI endpoint+method+auth-scope mining achieves strong alias-OOD resolution (39/40 0.975) on synthetic orthogonal header/body/auth + mixed multi-channel splits with minimal derived dict, statistically superior to exact-match (p<0.05) and verbatim replay (p<0.05), with calibrated ECE<=0.15 and no exact-match regression. HOWEVER, WebAPI provides ZERO complementarity advantage over flat TFIDF/EMBED K5+reconstruction, hierarchical retrieval, or even random retrieval (all 39/40, coverage 1.0, density ~1.38-1.71). The 'higher-leverage' claim vs hierarchical retrieval complementarity is FALSIFIED IN THIS SETTING. The reconstruction rule masks all retrieval differences. C-SEMANTIC-RESOLVE remains EXPERIMENTAL at rule-based reconstruction ceiling (39/40 synthetic), bounded to this synthetic substrate. No promotion to Product Core.

unresolved: Whether hierarchical vs WebAPI retrieval complementarity would emerge with reconstruction disabled (verbatim bind) or with weaker reconstruction requiring correct-family candidate. Current genuine reconstruction masks retrieval differences completely (random 39/40 = hierarchical = WebAPI = flat).

Whether coverage of correct alias-family component is the right complementarity construct once any candidate can be rewritten. Alternative metrics (distinct component types, entropy) also show no gain.

Live-browser generalization (WebShop/ALFWorld 1280x720, production SPA DOM/AX heterogeneity, auth/session drift, real endpoint discovery): N_live 0 for all pipelines. Synthetic-to-real gap remains dominant unknown.
Whether 84 themes (vs parent 63 singleton) indicates better grouping with expanded pool but still no coverage advantage. Jaccard threshold 0.6 specificity not tested post-hoc.
EMBED-K1 ablation shows 0.95 coverage with verbatim bind (vs 1.0 for K5+recon), suggesting retrieval alone has some signal but reconstruction dominates. Deeper ablation needed.

The single WebAPI failure (alias-2-7, auth heldout) is shared by hierarchical and flat. Whether this indicates a systematic gap in held-out auth generalization (X-Scope, permission, access_scope) or a registry expansion artifact.

Whether WebAPI endpoint mining would show advantage on real Fetch/WebMCP substrates with actual endpoint discovery (OpenAPI specs, HATEOAS, auth-scope negotiation) vs synthetic endpoint catalog derived from registry.
